title: 'My Josephine' and the call from King Oliver
summary: His composition 'My Josephine' made Celestin's band a hit, the record reached Chicago, and Oliver sent for him. He left in 1927 to join Oliver in St. Louis.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Jeanette Sullivan. So we got her to play in the band. And the band made a great success. The band then, I composed a number and we called it My Josephie. And the number made such a hit with the people that it actually swarmed Ridgely's Tuxedo. Really? By the way Ridgely called his band Ridgely's Tuxedo and Celestad called his band Papa Celestad's Tuxedo. But that Ridgely's Tuxedo band died out of the picture. And all that was left was Papa Celestad's Tuxedo band. So I stayed with Papa Celestad band. All that happened in 1925. And in 1927 that recording that I heard about, that I spoke to you about, My Josephine, when it got to Chicago, King Alba heard about the band. And the first thing he wondered who was that saxophone player doing all that play? Oh yeah. He wrote to a trumpet player called Manuel Perez. Manuel Perez and King Alba would be taking more musicians out of New Orleans than any other people. Because Manuel Perez would notice who was great. And the great ones he tells King Alba about.
And King Alba was simply. So then.
Yeah, you stayed with Celestan, that became the best band.

Yeah, well anyway I played with Celestan's band after that until 1927, and King Oliver had heard that record of my Josephine, and was so enthused over the work that I did that at the manual parades, told him about it, and I left Papa Celestan's band, that was in 1927, and I got there and joined King Oliver's band in St. Louis, Missouri, Red Island and I left together. And them fellas liked me because I showed them all, I showed Red Island a lot on his trumpet, and it's like I showed Celestan too, and they liked me very much for that. So anyway, we left Missouri, played there in St. Louis, Missouri, and we went to New York, played the Savoy Ballroom with King Oliver's band. You want to hear some of the line up of those bands?
